questions.question: A weak electrolyte is ______.
questions.solution: (c) NH4OH. NH4OH ionises only partially in water; alcohol and glucose are non-electrolytes and KOH is a strong electrolyte.

concepts: action of NH4OH on salt solutions
questions.question: Ranjan tested a salt solution by adding ammonium hydroxide dropwise, forming a dirty green precipitate. On adding excess ammonium hydroxide, the precipitate is insoluble. The cation present in the salt is:
questions.solution: (d) Iron (II) ion. Fe2+ gives a dirty green precipitate of Fe(OH)2 which is insoluble in excess NH4OH.

questions.question: Sulphur reacts with hot conc. nitric acid producing sulphuric acid, water and nitrogen dioxide. The property of nitric acid emphasised here is
questions.solution: (b) Oxidising nature. S + 6HNO3 -> H2SO4 + 2H2O + 6NO2; nitric acid oxidises sulphur to sulphuric acid.

questions.question:
In the electrolysis of acidified water, oxygen gas is produced at the anode. Which of the following ions moves towards the anode and will get discharged during this process?
X. Sulphate ion
Y. Hydroxide ion
Z. Oxide ion
questions.solution: (d) Only Y. SO4 2- and OH- both migrate to the anode, but only OH- is discharged (4OH- - 4e- -> 2H2O + O2) as it is lower in the discharge series.

concepts: passivity of Al with conc. HNO3
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aluminium does not react with nitric acid of any concentration.
Reason (R): A thin and unreactive protective layer of aluminium oxide forms on the surface of aluminium metal, preventing it from reacting with nitric acid.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation for A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (d) A is false, but R is true.. Concentrated nitric acid renders aluminium passive by forming a protective oxide layer (R true), but aluminium does react (slowly) with dilute nitric acid, so the statement 'of any concentration' makes A false.

questions.question:
The structures of four hydrocarbons are shown below:
A: H3C-CH=CH-Br (CH3-CH=CHBr)
B: H3C-C≡C-H (propyne)
C: H3C-CH2-C(=O)-O-H (CH3CH2COOH)
D: H3C-CH2-CH2-O-H (CH3CH2CH2OH)
Select the incorrect option

options.a: A, B and C are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
options.b: Only D is a saturated hydrocarbon.
options.c: A and B are not isomers.
options.d: B can be obtained from A by a dehydrobromination reaction.

questions.solution: (a) A, B and C are unsaturated hydrocarbons.. C is propanoic acid, a saturated (carboxylic acid) compound, not an unsaturated hydrocarbon. (c) is correct since A = C3H5Br and B = C3H4 have different formulae, and (d) is correct: CH3CH=CHBr + KOH(alc) -> CH3C≡CH + KBr + H2O. Note: strictly only B is a hydrocarbon (A, C and D contain Br/O), so option (b) is also loosely worded; (a) is the intended incorrect statement.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Ritika added acetic acid to test tubes I, II, III and IV containing the labelled substance and then brought a burning splinter near the mouth of each test tube.
I: NaOH; II: NaCl; III: NaHCO3; IV: Ca(OH)2
The splinter would be extinguished when brought near the mouth of the test tube:
questions.solution: (c) III. CH3COOH + NaHCO3 -> CH3COONa + H2O + CO2; carbon dioxide does not support combustion and puts out the splinter.

concepts: number of shells increases down a group
questions.question: The elements having the least number of electron shells:
questions.solution: (d) Li. Li (2,1) has only two shells; shells increase down the group.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Oxides of most metals are basic in nature.
Reason (R): They dissolve in water, forming hydroxide.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation for A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (c) A is true, but R is false.. Most metallic oxides are basic (they react with acids to form salt and water), but most are insoluble in water; only oxides of active metals like Na, K, Ca dissolve to form alkalis.

questions.topic: Period and group to shells and valence electrons
questions.question: An element A belonging to Period 3 and Group II will have:
questions.solution: (a) 3 shells and 2 valence electrons. Period number = number of shells (3); group II = 2 valence electrons (Mg: 2,8,2).

questions.question: The element that will have the highest ionisation potential is ______
questions.solution: (d) Helium. Helium has the smallest atom with a stable duplet held very close to the nucleus, so it has the highest ionisation potential of all elements.

questions.topic: Action of NaOH on salt solutions
concepts: amphoteric hydroxides dissolve in excess NaOH
questions.question:
Sodium hydroxide is added to the salt solutions, and shows different observations. Identify the correct set of observations from the given table:
| | Salt solution (precipitate) | Colour of precipitate | Solubility in excess of NaOH |
| W | Fe(OH)3 | Dirty green | Insoluble |
| X | Pb(OH)2 | White | Soluble |
| Y | Zn(OH)2 | White | Soluble |
questions.solution: (b) Both X and Y. Fe(OH)3 is reddish brown (not dirty green), so W is wrong; Pb(OH)2 (chalky white) and Zn(OH)2 (gelatinous white) both dissolve in excess NaOH.

questions.question: In the formation of sodium chloride, ______ loses the electron(s) to attain stable electronic configuration of ______.
questions.solution: (a) Sodium, neon. Na (2,8,1) loses one electron to become Na+ (2,8), the configuration of neon.

questions.question: A metal statue that was gifted to Arjun remained shiny and didn't rust, even after years. Arjun found out that the statue was made of a metal that is unaffected by dilute or concentrated acids. This metal is ______.
questions.solution: (d) Gold. Gold is a noble metal, least reactive, and is not attacked by dilute or concentrated acids (only by aqua regia); copper is attacked by conc. HNO3/H2SO4.

questions.topic: Electrorefining of zinc (zinc sulphate with zinc electrodes)
questions.question:
Zinc sulphate solution is electrolysed using zinc electrodes. Study the diagram carefully and answer the questions that follow.
[Diagram: D.C. power supply; left electrode = impure zinc connected to the + terminal (anode); right electrode = pure zinc connected to the - terminal (cathode); electrolyte = zinc sulphate solution (aq).]
(i) Identify whether the left electrode or the right electrode is the oxidising electrode. Give a reason for your answer. [2]
(ii) Write the balanced ionic equation for the reaction occurring at the electrode identified in part (i). [1]
(iii) State two observable changes that take place during the electrolysis - one at each electrode. [2]
questions.solution:
(i) The left electrode (impure zinc anode, connected to the positive terminal) is the oxidising electrode, because oxidation (loss of electrons) takes place at the anode - zinc atoms lose electrons and go into solution as Zn2+ ions.
(ii) Zn - 2e- -> Zn2+ (i.e. Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e-)
(iii) At the anode (left): the impure zinc electrode gets thinner / loses mass (impurities collect below as anode mud). At the cathode (right): pure zinc is deposited, the cathode becomes thicker / gains mass (greyish zinc layer).

marking_points.point: Reason: oxidation / loss of electrons occurs at anode (Zn -> Zn2+)
Cathode becomes thicker / zinc deposited on it

questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B.
Column A: a) Froth Flotation; b) Conc. Sulphuric Acid; c) Alkali metals; d) Carbon tetrachloride; e) CH3CHO
Column B: 1. Dehydrating agent; 2. Covalent compound; 3. Formaldehyde; 4. Sulphide ore; 5. Electrovalent compound; 6. Li, K, Na, Rb
questions.solution: a-4 (froth flotation concentrates sulphide ores); b-1 (conc. H2SO4 is a dehydrating agent); c-6 (Li, K, Na, Rb are alkali metals); d-2 (CCl4 is a covalent compound); e-3 (intended match: aldehyde. Note: CH3CHO is actually acetaldehyde/ethanal; formaldehyde is HCHO). Option 5 is the extra distractor.

questions.question:
Complete the following by choosing the correct answers from the brackets:
(i) If an element has seven valence electrons, then it is likely to have the ______ [smallest/largest] electron affinity among all the elements in the same period.
(ii) The higher the pH value of a solution, the more ______ [alkaline/acidic] it is.
(iii) A ______ [reddish brown/dirty green] coloured precipitate is formed when ammonium hydroxide is added to a solution of ferric chloride.
(iv) Alkanes undergo ______ [addition/substitution] reactions.
(v) The indicator which does not change colour on passage of HCl gas is ______ [methyl orange, moist blue litmus, phenolphthalein]

answer_items.prompt: (i) electron affinity of element with 7 valence electrons
(iii) colour of precipitate with ferric chloride + NH4OH
(v) indicator that does not change colour with HCl gas

questions.solution:
(i) largest (halogens have the highest electron affinity in their period)
(ii) alkaline
(iii) reddish brown (Fe(OH)3)
(iv) substitution (alkanes are saturated)
(v) phenolphthalein (remains colourless in acidic medium; methyl orange turns pink/red and blue litmus turns red)

questions.question:
Identify the following:
(i) A polar covalent compound, but when dissolved in water, it conducts electricity.
(ii) A salt formed by the incomplete neutralisation of an acid by a base.
(iii) A sweet-smelling compound is formed when ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid.
(iv) The gas that turns acidified potassium dichromate green.
(v) The process of heating the concentrated ore in the absence of or with a limited supply of air at a temperature not sufficient to melt the ore.

answer_items.prompt: (i) Polar covalent compound that conducts when dissolved in water
(ii) Salt from incomplete neutralisation of an acid
(iii) Sweet-smelling compound from ethanol + ethanoic acid
(iv) Gas that turns acidified K2Cr2O7 green
(v) Heating ore in absence/limited air below melting point

questions.solution:
(i) Hydrogen chloride (HCl) - polar covalent, but ionises in water (H3O+ and Cl-)
(ii) Acid salt (e.g. NaHSO4)
(iii) Ethyl ethanoate (ester, CH3COOC2H5)
(iv) Sulphur dioxide (SO2)
(v) Calcination

questions.question:
Draw the structural diagrams for the following compounds:
(a) 3-Bromo-3-methylbutanal
(b) 2-Methyl prop-1-ene
(c) Propanoic acid
questions.solution:
(a) 3-Bromo-3-methylbutanal: OHC-CH2-C(Br)(CH3)-CH3, i.e. H-C(=O)-CH2-C(Br)(CH3)-CH3 - a 4-carbon chain with the aldehyde carbon as C1, and both a Br and a CH3 on C3; all C-H bonds shown.
(b) 2-Methylprop-1-ene: CH2=C(CH3)-CH3 - a double bond between C1 and C2 with a CH3 branch on C2.
(c) Propanoic acid: CH3-CH2-C(=O)-O-H with all bonds shown.

(b) CH3-CH2-C(OH)(Br)-CH3

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: State why the basicity of acetic acid is one and the acidity of calcium hydroxide is two.
questions.solution: Acetic acid (CH3COOH) has only one replaceable (ionisable) hydrogen ion per molecule: CH3COOH ⇌ CH3COO- + H+, so its basicity is 1. Calcium hydroxide gives two hydroxide ions per molecule: Ca(OH)2 -> Ca2+ + 2OH-, so its acidity is 2.

marking_points.point: Acetic acid has one ionisable/replaceable H+ per molecule
Ca(OH)2 gives two OH- ions per molecule

questions.topic: Moles and gas volume from equation
questions.question:
Concentrated nitric acid oxidises phosphorus to phosphoric acid according to the following equation:
P + 5HNO3 (conc.) -> H3PO4 + H2O + 5NO2
If 9.3 g of phosphorus were used in the reaction, calculate:
(a) Number of moles of phosphorus taken.
(b) The volume of nitrogen dioxide produced at STP. [H = 1, N = 14, P = 31, O = 16]
questions.solution:
(a) Moles of P = 9.3 / 31 = 0.3 mol
(b) 1 mol P gives 5 mol NO2, so 0.3 mol P gives 1.5 mol NO2.
Volume at STP = 1.5 x 22.4 = 33.6 dm3 (33.6 litres)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Propane burns in air according to the following equation.
C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O
What volume of propane is consumed on using 1000 cm3 of air, considering only 40% of the air contains oxygen?
questions.solution:
Volume of oxygen = 40% of 1000 cm3 = 400 cm3.
By Gay-Lussac's law, 1 vol C3H8 : 5 vol O2.
Volume of propane = 400 / 5 = 80 cm3.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The structures of six organic compounds are shown below:
A: CH3-CH=CH2
B: CH3-OH
C: CH3-CH(OH)-CH3
D: CH3-CH2-Cl (H-C(Cl)(H)-C(H)(H)-H)
E: CH3-CH2-CH2-OH
F: CH3-CHO (H-C(H)(H)-C(=O)-H)
(a) Identify two of the compounds that are members of the same homologous series but are not isomers.
(b) Which compound belongs to the homologous series having the general formula CnH2n?
(c) Compound E can be prepared from D. Give a chemical equation for the reaction.
questions.solution:
(a) B and C (or B and E) - all are alcohols; B (methanol, CH4O) differs from C/E (C3H8O), so they are not isomers. (C and E are isomers of each other.)
(b) A (propene, alkene, CnH2n)
(c) Alcohols are prepared by boiling a haloalkane with aqueous KOH/NaOH (hydrolysis). As printed, D is chloroethane, whose hydrolysis gives ethanol: C2H5Cl + KOH(aq) -> C2H5OH + KCl. To obtain E (propan-1-ol) the haloalkane must be 1-chloropropane: CH3CH2CH2Cl + KOH(aq) -> CH3CH2CH2OH + KCl. (Note: the paper's D has only two carbons, so it cannot directly give E; credit the hydrolysis equation.)

marking_points.point: B and C (or B and E)
Correct balanced hydrolysis equation of haloalkane with aqueous KOH/NaOH

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Absorption of SO3 in conc. H2SO4
questions.question: SO3 vapours are absorbed in conc. H2SO4 and not in water. Explain.
questions.solution: SO3 reacts with water in a highly exothermic reaction; the heat vaporises the water and produces a dense fog/mist of sulphuric acid droplets which does not condense easily, so absorption is incomplete. Hence SO3 is dissolved in conc. H2SO4 to form oleum: SO3 + H2SO4 -> H2S2O7, which is then diluted with water: H2S2O7 + H2O -> 2H2SO4.

marking_points.point: Reaction with water is highly exothermic forming dense acid mist/fog that does not condense
SO3 + H2SO4 -> H2S2O7 (oleum), then diluted to H2SO4

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Answer the following questions based on the laboratory preparation of nitric acid:
(a) Reactants used for the manufacture of nitric acid.
(b) Give a balanced chemical equation for the preparation of nitric acid.
(c) The method of collection of the acid.
(d) Why should the temperature of the reaction mixture of nitric acid not be allowed to rise above 200 °C?
questions.solution:
(a) Potassium nitrate (or sodium nitrate) and concentrated sulphuric acid.
(b) KNO3 + H2SO4 (conc.) -> KHSO4 + HNO3 (below 200 °C)
(c) Nitric acid vapours are condensed and collected in a receiver (flask) kept cooled under running water.
(d) At higher temperature nitric acid decomposes (4HNO3 -> 2H2O + 4NO2 + O2), and the residue K2SO4 forms a hard crust that is difficult to remove and can damage the glass apparatus; also more fuel is wasted.

marking_points.point: Vapours condensed in a water-cooled receiver
Nitric acid decomposes / hard crust of K2SO4 damages apparatus

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: An organic compound containing C, H and O has 49.3% carbon, 6.84% hydrogen, 43.86% oxygen and its vapour density is 73. What will be the molecular formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
C: 49.3/12 = 4.108; H: 6.84/1 = 6.84; O: 43.86/16 = 2.741
Divide by smallest (2.741): C = 1.5, H = 2.5, O = 1
Multiply by 2: C : H : O = 3 : 5 : 2 -> empirical formula C3H5O2
Empirical formula mass = 36 + 5 + 32 = 73
Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 2 x 73 = 146
n = 146/73 = 2 -> molecular formula C6H10O4

marking_points.point: Molecular mass = 2 x VD = 146; EF mass 73

questions.topic: Distinguishing salts using NaOH and NH4OH
questions.question:
Distinguish by adding NaOH solution and NH4OH solution to:
(a) Calcium salt solution and lead salt solution
(b) Lead nitrate solution and zinc nitrate solution
questions.solution:
(a) With NaOH: calcium salt gives a white precipitate of Ca(OH)2 that is (sparingly soluble /) insoluble in excess NaOH; lead salt gives a chalky white precipitate of Pb(OH)2 that dissolves in excess NaOH. With NH4OH: calcium salt gives no precipitate; lead salt gives a chalky white precipitate insoluble in excess.
(b) With NaOH both give white precipitates soluble in excess, so use NH4OH: lead nitrate gives a chalky white precipitate insoluble in excess NH4OH; zinc nitrate gives a white gelatinous precipitate that dissolves in excess NH4OH (forming [Zn(NH3)4]2+).

marking_points.point: Ca vs Pb: Pb(OH)2 soluble in excess NaOH while Ca(OH)2 is not / Ca gives no ppt with NH4OH
Pb vs Zn: Zn(OH)2 soluble in excess NH4OH, Pb(OH)2 insoluble

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Berzelius used the following methods for the preparation of salts.
[Neutralisation, Displacement, Precipitation, Neutralisation by titration]
The list of salts is given below. Identify the most appropriate method from the list given above for their preparation.
(a) Potassium hydroxide + Hydrochloric acid
(b) Barium chloride + Sodium hydroxide
(c) Magnesium + Hydrochloric acid
